title: Rhodesia
capsule: Rhodesia was the unrecognized white-minority state in the territory of present-day Zimbabwe, between the Zambezi and Limpopo rivers, that arose from Ian Smith's Rhodesian Front government's Unilateral Declaration of Independence on 11 November 1965 in defiance of British demands for majority rule. After a 1969 referendum it severed its last ties to the Crown and became the Republic of Rhodesia on 2 March 1970, governing under international sanctions while fighting a protracted bush war against the ZANU and ZAPU guerrilla movements. The conflict drove the country toward the 1979 Internal Settlement and brief reconstitution as Zimbabwe Rhodesia; the Lancaster House Agreement of December 1979 then returned it to temporary British control ahead of the 1980 elections that created Zimbabwe.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territory precisely defined by colonial boundaries; sovereignty was disputed (not recognized internationally) but physical extent is unambiguous.
